title: Matplotlib Introduction and Installation
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and main concepts of Matplotlib Introduction and Installation.
Create a Matplotlib Figure and Axes suitable for the visualization task.
Apply the relevant plotting API and configure its key properties.
Inspect plotted artists or chart properties to verify the intended result.
Choose labels and visual encodings that communicate data accurately.
prerequisites: NumPy arrays and basic numeric data

understand.concept: Matplotlib is a Python library for creating static, animated and interactive visualizations. Its pyplot interface offers familiar plotting commands, while Figure and Axes objects provide explicit control. A non-interactive backend such as Agg is useful for automated validation and file export.
understand.whyItMatters: Visualizations help communicate patterns, comparisons and distributions, but a chart is only useful when its data and labels are correct.
understand.analogy: A Figure is the page or canvas; an Axes object is the plotting area placed on that page.
understand.summary: Matplotlib Introduction and Installation is part of the Matplotlib learning path. The examples use deterministic data and the Agg backend for automated execution.

explain.narrative: Read the concept, execute each example in sequence, inspect the printed result and compare it with the expected output. Each example creates a figure with the non-interactive Agg backend and closes it after inspection.

examples.title: Inspect the installed version
examples.explanation: The CI environment pins Matplotlib 3.10.8 so examples are reproducible.

examples.title: Create a plotting area
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
print(type(ax).__name__)
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: subplots returns a Figure and an Axes object.

examples.title: Inspect the default figure size
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
print(fig.get_size_inches().tolist())
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: The default figure size is measured in inches.

examples.title: Use a non-interactive canvas
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
print(type(fig.canvas).__name__)
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: Agg renders figures without requiring a desktop window.

examples.title: Draw a first line
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot([1, 2, 3], [2, 4, 6])
print(len(ax.lines))
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: plot adds a Line2D object to the Axes.

practise.guidedTask: Create a small program demonstrating matplotlib introduction and installation. Use a deterministic dataset, configure the relevant chart properties, and print at least one check that verifies the result.
practise.independentTask: Apply the technique to a small dataset of your own. Include meaningful labels, check input lengths and explain why the chosen chart is appropriate.
hints: Start with a small deterministic dataset.
Create the Figure and Axes explicitly with plt.subplots().
Inspect the relevant artist or Axes property instead of relying on visual output alone.
Add labels and units that accurately describe the data.
Close figures after automated checks or file export.
practise.challenge: Build a reusable plotting function that validates its inputs, creates the requested chart, and returns or saves a well-labelled Figure without leaking open figures.
validationCriteria: All five examples execute under the pinned Python and Matplotlib environment and match expected output.
Examples use the intended Matplotlib API correctly.
The chart type and visual encodings match the data semantics.
Labels, legends and scales are accurate and readable where applicable.
Figures are closed after automated execution.

A Figure contains one or more Axes.

questions.prompt: What does an Axes object represent?
questions.answer: A plotting area with axes and plotted artists
options: A plotting area with axes and plotted artists

questions.answer: It renders without opening a GUI window
options: It renders without opening a GUI window
